title: Lesson 2: Working Together Is Not the Same as Working in the Same Place
summary: Sharing a workplace is not teamwork. Teamwork means looking beyond your own task and considering how your actions affect colleagues and clients.

items.label: Day
items.body: 1 — Understanding Teamwork and the Zura Team Culture

items.label: Focus
items.body: The difference between working together and simply working in the same place

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: Staff can work in the same building, on the same shift, and still not be a team.
Working in the same place only means people occupy the same space. Teamwork means they cooperate, communicate, support one another and take responsibility for a shared result.
At Zura Spa, a client's experience depends on more than one person completing their own list. It depends on whether staff notice what the next person needs and act accordingly.

sections.title: Scenario A: Poor teamwork
paragraphs: A therapist finishes a session and notices that another treatment room needs preparation before the next client arrives.
She has completed her assigned work, so she ignores the situation, even though she has time to help.
The next client arrives and has to wait.
When management asks what happened, she responds, "That is not my responsibility."
Result: Delayed service, unnecessary pressure on colleagues and a poor client experience.

sections.title: Scenario B: Good teamwork
paragraphs: A therapist finishes her session and notices that another treatment room needs preparation.
She checks whether her colleague needs assistance and offers to help, provided it does not interfere with her own responsibilities.
The room is prepared on time, and the next client receives prompt service.
Result: Better service, reduced pressure and stronger working relationships.

sections.title: 3. The lesson
paragraphs: Good teamwork requires people to look beyond their individual tasks and consider how their actions affect others.
However, teamwork does not mean doing another person's work continuously or allowing colleagues to neglect their responsibilities.
Support is part of teamwork. Covering for repeated neglect is not.

items.label: Working in the same place
items.body: Each person completes only their own list, ignores gaps that affect the next client, and says "that is not my job" when help is possible.

items.label: Working together
items.body: Each person owns their duties, notices what the team needs, offers reasonable help, and communicates so the client is not left waiting.

remember: Sharing a shift is not teamwork. Teamwork is cooperating so the next client, and the next colleague, are not left with your gap.
